A source with the potential to cause harm (energy, substance, condition, behaviour).
Combination of the likelihood of harm and its severity; rated on a matrix before and after controls.
Systematic process to identify hazards, evaluate risk and decide controls (HIRA/JSA/HAZOP).
As Low As Reasonably Practicable — reduce risk until further reduction is grossly disproportionate to cost.
Elimination → substitution → engineering → administrative → PPE; the order of preference for controls.
A behaviour that departs from safe practice and can cause an incident (e.g., removing a guard).
A physical state of the workplace or equipment that can cause an incident (e.g., missing guardrail).
An unplanned event that did not cause injury or damage but could have; a free lesson.
Incident: any unplanned event that did or could cause harm; accident: an incident with injury/damage.
Listed serious event (collapse, explosion, fire, pressure burst, release) reportable even without injury (OSH Code s.11).
Work injury causing absence beyond the day of injury (India: absence ≥ 48 h triggers statutory notice).
OSHA: injury needing medical treatment beyond first aid, restricted work, days away, loss of consciousness or death.
Minor treatment (cleaning, dressing, cold pack) with no further medical care; recorded in the first-aid register.
Death from a work-related injury or illness; reported forthwith to ICF, police and family.
Illness caused by work exposure (silicosis, NIHL, dermatitis, lead poisoning); notifiable under OSH Code s.12.
Person with training, knowledge and experience (and statutory recognition where required) to perform a task or inspection.
Person appointed in writing to perform a specific duty (e.g., HT switching, permit issue).
Person responsible for planning lifting operations (BS 7121).
Legal obligation to take reasonable care to avoid harm to others; employer's general duties (OSH Code s.6).
Person with ultimate control of the factory/establishment (legally accountable under OSH Code).
The establishment that engages contractors; liable for contract workers' welfare and safety if the contractor defaults.
Formal procedure resulting from systematic examination of a task to identify hazards and define safe methods.
Step-by-step description of how a task will be done safely, with hazards and controls.

Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment — the site/plant-level risk register.
Hazard and Operability study — guide-word-based review of process deviations (IEC 61882).

Diagram linking threats, preventive barriers, the top event, mitigative barriers and consequences.
Brainstorm-based hazard review for simpler processes.
Risk remaining after controls; must be within acceptance criteria.
Grid of likelihood vs severity used to rate risk (e.g., 5×5).
Accidents occur when holes in successive layers of defence align (Reason).
Ratio model: many unsafe acts/near misses for each serious injury.
Finding the underlying management-system causes of an incident (5-Why, fishbone, TapRooT, ICAM).

Leading: inspections, training, near-miss reports, observations; lagging: injuries, LTIFR, severity rate.

Combined index √(FR × SR) sometimes used in Indian safety awards.

Structured watching of work with feedback on safe and at-risk behaviours (BBS).

Shared values and practices about safety (culture) and the current perception of them (climate).
Visible, consistent management involvement in safety (walks, conversations).
Short daily briefing at the workface on tasks, hazards and controls.
Mandatory orientation on site hazards, rules and emergency arrangements before first entry.

Controlling hours, shift patterns and rest to prevent impaired alertness.

Engineered ground mat supporting rigs; certified before use.

Rigging hardware; load in line, pin seated, rated for the load.
